items.title: A finite set of points whose traces on each irreducible component lie in an affine open lies in an affine open
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma assembles the per-component affine containment hypotheses into a single affine open containing the whole finite set T. The proof proceeds by induction on the number of irreducible components: given an affine open U meeting the first r-1 components in the desired way and an affine open V inside the r-th component containing T cap Z_r, one shows that Delta = (U cap Z_r) minus (U cap V) is closed in U and contains no point of T, and then uses prime avoidance to replace U by a standard open U' containing T cap U and disjoint from Delta, so that U cap V becomes closed in U; a symmetric argument handles the remaining components (proof lines 9094-9135). H2: the two prime-avoidance steps that make the intersections closed are the substance.
